chunks: 1031 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from al-Ribati, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said:
I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying:

"Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, caused His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله to sleep through salat al-fajr until the sun rose. Then he stood and began, so he prayed the two rak'ahs that are before al-fajr, then he prayed al-fajr. And He caused him to forget in his salat, so he gave salutation after two rak'ahs. Then he described what Dhu al-Shimalayn said. He only did that to him as a mercy for this ummah, so that the Muslim man would not be reproached when he sleeps through his salat or forgets in it, and it would be said: that happened to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله."

key_terms.أَسْهَاهُ: caused him to forget during the prayer
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two units of prayer mentioned before the obligatory Fajr prayer
key_terms.الْأُمَّةِ: the Muslim community addressed by this legal and spiritual mercy
key_terms.رَحْمَةً: a mercy and easing granted for this community
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.سَهَا: forgot or erred within the prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ: the dawn prayer, the obligatory morning salat

ai.seo_question: Why does this hadith say the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله slept through Fajr and forgot in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, caused the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله to sleep through salat al-fajr and to forget within the prayer as a mercy for the ummah. Its significance is to establish that when a Muslim oversleeps a prayer or experiences forgetfulness in salat, he should not be shamed, since such an occurrence was made to happen to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
